reform_description: Union Budget 1991-92: ad valorem customs peak capped at 150% (previously >300% on some lines)
Tariff cuts on 3,596 duty codes in Jan and Dec 1992 (avg -7.3%); 1986-91 cuts had touched only 81 of ~6300 codes
WTO TPR 2000: 'Since 1992 Bangladesh has continued to liberalize... greatly reducing tariffs'; bands 15 (1992/93) -> 5 (1999/2000); max tariff 300% -> 37.5%; avg MFN 58% -> 22%
After taking office in 1997 the government cut the maximum tariff from 65% to 45%; to 35% in March 1999 (SPDC budget evaluation); WTO TPR 2002 confirms max rate 30% then 25%
Executive Order 264 (signed 22 Jul 1995): industrial tariff reduction programme in effect from 28 Aug 1995 (per EO 288 recital)
WTO TPR 2000: max ad valorem rate lowered from 60% in 1992 to 25% in 1999; bands 8 (1994) -> 5
WAEMU Common External Tariff (4 rates: 1/6/11/21%): transition began July 1998, completed Jan 2000 (WTO TPR Togo 1999). Same reform as SEN.
WAEMU Common External Tariff: transition began July 1998, completed Jan 2000 (WTO TPR Togo 1999). Same reform as CIV.
No open source found that dates a tariff-cutting reform. WTO TPR 2001 still reports MFN rates up to 65% in 2000/01 Budget and ~20% average.
No open source found that dates a tariff-cutting reform. WTO TPR 1999 reports tariff INCREASES during 1995-99 review period, so a 1995 date could not be confirmed.
